title: Barcelona win Women’s Champions League with 4-0 victory over Lyon: How poetic Pajor secured title
content:
Barcelona regained the Women’s Champions League title with a 4-0 win over Lyon in Saturday’s final.

Striker Eva Pajor and forward Salma Paralluelo both scored twice in the second half at the Ullevaal stadium in Oslo, Norway, to ensure the Spanish side were crowned European champions for the fourth time in six years. Goalkeeper Cata Coll pulled off several important saves to keep Lyon at bay, with Paralluelo finding the net in quick succession in the 90th and 93rd minutes to give the result a more emphatic look.

The game, a repeat of the competition’s 2019, 2022 and 2024 finals, was Barca’s sixth successive appearance in this fixture, but it was Lyon who enjoyed the better of the first half. USWNT midfielder Lindsey Heaps thought she had given the French champions the lead in the 13th minute when she side-footed home after Wendie Renard’s header was palmed into her path by Coll, but the goal was ruled out for offside following a VAR review.

Barcelona’s best chance of the half fell to Pajor, who hit the side netting after lobbing goalkeeper Christiane Endler, but this was a rare sight of goal for them in the opening 45 minutes.

Selma Bacha had a free kick well saved by Coll before the break, and the Barca goalkeeper also denied Ada Hegerberg from close range early in the second half.

Barcelona opened the scoring shortly after, Pajor firing low into the bottom corner after being found by Patri Guijarro. The Poland international doubled their advantage in the 69th minute, prodding home from close range after being teed up by Paralluelo.

Tabitha Chawinga had an opportunity to halve the deficit when she was put through one-v-one, but again could not find a way past Coll.

Paralluelo put the game beyond Lyon with two more goals on the cusp of full time, the first a superb solo strike from distance and the second stroking home from inside the penalty area.

Analysis from women’s soccer writer Tamerra Griffin

The poetry of Pajor’s two goals, and first Champions League title after six failed attempts at a continental title, is worthy of Polish folklore.

Her first, in the 55th minute, might have been enough to seal Barcelona’s victory. Lyon retreated slightly at the start of the second half compared to the opening 45 minutes, as though they were short of a Plan B. Barcelona, meanwhile, began the half apparently having rid themselves of what wasn’t working in the first — assuming they could out-possess Lyon and enjoy their time on the ball — and leaning into what was. They supplemented their need for the ball with a need to simplify, which was what made Guijarro’s through ball to Pajor fundamentally brilliant.

Her second was also evocative of Barcelona’s ethos of sublime composure on the ball, no matter the context. Even after jigsawing their way into Lyon’s penalty box and seeing a cross put inches wide, Paralluelo had the patience and presence of mind to put her foot on the ball and just… wait. That extra second was enough to further throw off Lyon’s defence and give Pajor enough time to prepare herself to score a dagger of a second goal.

Heaps’ frustration with her side’s performance — beginning in the second half, and particularly after Lyon failed to capitalize on the attacking chances they created — grew increasingly passionate as the game carried on. They had done well to create promising chances for themselves across both halves but the disparity between the quality of attacking players they have and the lack of finishing from them in this game was stark.

Barcelona’s first and second goals had a tightening effect on their ambitions. In the first half, they were tentative in front of goal, but as is often the case with the Catalan side, their confidence is contagious. Why not go for more?

And why not 22-year-old Paralluelo to score them? The Spanish forward’s brace in the final minutes — one a gorgeous long-range shot, the other a clinical finish, both with her left foot — could be read as an optimistic message to Barcelona supporters.

As they await news on the future of their queen, Alexia Putellas, with bated breath, Paralluelo’s pair of goals on Saturday is a reminder that this team also possesses invaluable depth.
